description: Let the phone accept Claude's/the shell's inline autocomplete (greyed ghost text): teach the terminal-key layer the Right-arrow (and End) CSI accept sequences, wire a press_right quick-action through the Mac injector, and add a compact accept-suggestion control to the iOS input row. Pure CSI-byte logic lives in a new Foundation-only Shared helper gated by a swiftc assertion harness (tools/run-accept-autocomplete-tests.sh) so the autonomous loop needs no Xcode, simulator, or signing; the AppKit/SwiftUI wiring is grep-verified in the loop and integration-built by a human.

userStories.title: Add Shared terminal-key CSI table
userStories.description: As a Quip developer, I want a Foundation-only helper that maps arrow/navigation key names to their raw ANSI CSI byte sequences, so both peers and the Mac injector share one authoritative source for the bytes that accept an autocomplete suggestion.
acceptanceCriteria: Create Shared/TerminalKeyBytes.swift (import Foundation only, no AppKit/UIKit/SwiftUI) exposing TerminalKeyBytes.csi(for key: String) -> String? returning the raw escape sequence for a key name.
csi(for:) returns \u{1B}[A for "up", \u{1B}[B for "down", \u{1B}[C for "right", \u{1B}[D for "left", and \u{1B}[F for "end"; it is case-insensitive and returns nil for an unknown key.
"right" is documented in-code as the primary accept-autocomplete key (zsh-autosuggestions / fish / Claude Code inline suggest), with "end" noted as the alternate.
Create tools/run-accept-autocomplete-tests.sh that compiles Shared/TerminalKeyBytes.swift plus a Foundation-only assertion harness with swiftc and runs it, exiting non-zero on any failed assertion.
The harness asserts csi("right") == "\u{1B}[C", csi("RIGHT") == "\u{1B}[C" (case-insensitive), csi("end") == "\u{1B}[F", and csi("bogus") == nil.
bash tools/run-accept-autocomplete-tests.sh exits 0 with all US-001 assertions passing.

userStories.title: Teach injector the Right-arrow key
userStories.description: As a Quip developer, I want the Mac KeystrokeInjector to emit a Right-arrow across its iTerm2 write-text and CGEvent paths, so a press-right request reaches the terminal as a real arrow key on the platforms multiselect navigation already supports.
acceptanceCriteria: KeystrokeInjector.iTerm2WriteExpression(for:) returns the AppleScript expression for "right" as ((character id 27) & "[C"), matching the existing up/down entries in shape and derivable from TerminalKeyBytes.csi(for: "right").
KeystrokeInjector's virtual-key map (keyCodeFor) returns 124 for "right" (macOS Right-arrow keycode), alongside the existing down=125/up=126 entries.
Add a "right" case assertion to QuipMac/Tests/KeystrokeInjectorWriteExpressionTests.swift locking the AppleScript expression, consistent with how up/down are asserted.
grep confirms iTerm2WriteExpression and keyCodeFor in QuipMac/Services/KeystrokeInjector.swift both handle "right".
bash tools/run-accept-autocomplete-tests.sh exits 0 (US-001 + US-002 harness assertions pass).

Human integration gate noted: run xcodebuild test -project QuipMac/QuipMac.xcodeproj -scheme QuipMac -only-testing:QuipMacTests/KeystrokeInjectorWriteExpressionTests -destination 'platform=macOS' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO after an xcodegen generate (zero-pbxproj protocol).

userStories.title: Wire Mac press_right quick-action
userStories.description: As a Quip user, I want a phone action that makes the Mac press Right-arrow in the focused terminal, so tapping accept sends the keystroke that commits the shown autocomplete suggestion.
acceptanceCriteria: QuipMac/QuipMacApp.swift handleQuickAction gains a case "press_right" that calls keystrokeInjector.sendKeystroke("right", ...) with the same window/session arguments as the existing press_tab / press_escape cases.
The case runs through the existing runAfterDelay focus path so the arrow lands after the window is raised, matching the other press_* actions.
grep confirms QuipMacApp.swift dispatches "press_right" to sendKeystroke("right").
bash tools/run-accept-autocomplete-tests.sh exits 0 (US-001..US-003 harness assertions pass).
Human integration gate noted: rebuild QuipMac and confirm a press_right from the phone advances the cursor / accepts a shell autosuggestion in the focused terminal.

userStories.title: Add iOS accept-suggestion control
userStories.description: As a Quip user, I want a compact accept-autocomplete button in the input row, so when Claude shows greyed ghost text I can commit it from the phone with one tap instead of retyping.
acceptanceCriteria: QuipiOS/QuipApp.swift adds a TerminalActionKey case (e.g. .acceptAutocomplete) that maps to .quickAction("press_right"), alongside the existing .tab / .esc / .shiftTab cases.
The action appears in the phone's terminal action list (the [(label, action)] table near the other press_* entries) with a clear label such as "Accept autocomplete".

A compact icon button (e.g. arrow.right.to.line / text.append) is added to the existing input control row and sends the press_right quick-action via onSendAction; it introduces no new fixed row and follows the compact-UI rule.
grep confirms QuipApp.swift wires the new key to quickAction("press_right") and renders a button that sends it.
bash tools/run-accept-autocomplete-tests.sh exits 0 (US-001..US-004 harness assertions pass).

Human UI gate noted: install QuipiOS and confirm the button accepts a live autosuggestion; if Right-arrow does not accept on the target prompt, swap the mapped key to "end" (already supported by TerminalKeyBytes) — a one-line change.
